review_notes: I read the whole file. I searched Mathlib/Combinatorics and the SimpleGraph directory for other disjoint-sum or disjoint-union graph constructions. I also searched for other sumComm, sumAssoc, sumCongr, Hom.sum and Embedding.sum declarations, and for other colouring-of-sum constructions. The only other uses of the sum graph are in Prod.lean, where `sumBoxProdDistrib` consumes `⊕g` and is not a competitor. Bipartite.lean and Coloring/Vertex.lean use `Sum.elim` and `Sum.inl` only for specific proofs about complete bipartite graphs. No independent graph-level sum with the same meaning exists elsewhere. The Hom, Embedding and Iso wrappers, `Coloring.sum`, `sumLeft`, `sumRight` and `sumEquiv`, and `edgeSetSumEquiv` are named specialisations over `Sum.map`, `Sum.elim` and `Equiv.sumCongr`. They are not competing definitions. I found no concrete case for consolidating any of them.
